title: Experimental Quickledger — Tess
content:
Purpose: compact personal tracker for quick micro-runs — single-sheet snapshot I keep on my laptop while iterating on batching/kv-cache heuristics. Use this to decide which variants to roll to nightly and which to drop.

Notes to self:
- Keep runs short (<= 5000 tokens steady-state) for cost comparability.
- Compare p50/p95 and cost per 10k tokens. Watch for tail regressions when cache hit drops below 70%.
- TODO: add inference-load profile script that simulates sliding-window chat.

Run table (columns: run_id | date | model | quant | bs | seq | kv_cache | p50_ms | p95_ms | tok_cost_per_1k | notes):

R001 | 2026-02-18 | ggml-redwood-7b | int8 | 8 | 512 | on (hits ~82%) | 34 | 72 | $0.18 | baseline small-batch, good stability
R002 | 2026-02-20 | ggml-redwood-7b | int8 | 16 | 512 | on (hits ~78%) | 42 | 98 | $0.12 | throughput up, tail worse after 200 concurrent reqs
R003 | 2026-02-22 | rwx-7b-v2 | q4_0 | 8 | 1024 | off | 58 | 140 | $0.14 | quality check, higher latency expected
R004 | 2026-02-25 | rwx-7b-v2 | q4_0 | 8 | 1024 | on (warm cache) | 45 | 95 | $0.14 | cache warm helped p95 a lot
R005 | 2026-03-02 | rdx-13b | int8 | 4 | 2048 | on (hits ~65%) | 128 | 280 | $0.85 | costy — consider smaller ctx or quant tweak
R006 | 2026-03-05 | rdx-13b | q4_0 | 4 | 2048 | on (hits ~70%) | 112 | 240 | $0.62 | q4_0 helps; check for regression in rare tokens
R007 | 2026-03-08 | rwx-7b-v2 | int8 | 12 | 512 | on (hits ~88%) | 38 | 80 | $0.10 | best cost/latency so far, stable under burst
R008 | 2026-03-10 | rwx-7b-v2 | int8 | 12 | 512 | on (cold start) | 86 | 210 | $0.10 | cold starts spike p95 — investigate pre-warm policy

Quick observations and micro-actions:
- When kv_cache_hits > 80% latency savings are ~25-40% for rwx-7b-v2; aim for >80% with small session pinning.
- For 13B runs, q4_0 reduces cost ~25% with small latency improvement; check output-token-level perplexity on eval prompt set before promoting.
- Batch size sweet spot for 7B int8 seems 8–12 depending on concurrency. Higher bs reduces unit cost but increases burst p95.
- Pre-warm strategy: 5-10 warm requests to maintain cache for known session cohorts — try scheduled keepalive at 15s.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Q1: Does sliding-window context (re-encoding last 256 tokens) reduce cache hit and how does it change cost curve? (experiment: simulate 60k chat turns, measure hit% over time)
- Q2: Can a tiny local LRU for prefixes (50MB) improve cold-start p95 for short sessions? (proto: local cache layer + fallback)
- Q3: Is there measurable quality drop for q4_0 on rare-token-heavy prompts? (eval set: legal/medical snippets)

Quick checkpoints (what I want to see before promoting a variant):
- p95 within 2x of baseline under expected concurrency profile
- token-cost reduction >= 15% with no quality regressions flagged by eval harness
- cold-start p95 improved by pre-warm or accept tradeoff documented

Scratch snippets (logs + commands):
- perf-run.sh --model=rwx-7b-v2 --quant=int8 --bs=12 --seq=512 --concurrency=200 --duration=300 > r007-run.log
- jq '.metrics | {p50, p95, tok_cost}' r007-run.json
- GH PR: repo/inference/runtime#2410 (kv-cache heuristics change) — review notes from Ravi on eviction timing

Mini-retrospective (2026-03-11):
- Wins: rwx-7b-v2 int8 at bs=12 looks like a low-cost default for interactive chat.
- Risks: cold starts and 13B cost remain blockers for moving to general default.
- Next week: run Q1 sliding-window sim and a targeted q4_0 eval on 500 legal prompts.

Freeform notes: 
- Keep this sheet lean. If a run looks promising, snapshot to a per-variant sheet under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/runs/ for team visibility.
- Ping @ravi in Slack when I have the sliding-window sim results.

End of quickledger.
